# flac-lite GAFP asset facts -- GENERATED
# DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Regenerate with: scripts/gen_gafp_fixtures.py
# Packer: scripts/gafp_pack.py (the real GAFP writer, item 6b-2).
# Frame walk: scripts/frame_vectors.py find_frames/parse_frame_header -- strict
#   RFC 9639 9.1 header + verifying CRC-8, never a bare sync scan; subframe walk:
#   gafp_pack.walk_subframe. Source PCM: scripts/frame_vectors.py synth_pcm
#   (integer-exact, no RNG). Reference PCM: `flac -d` of the stream the frames
#   came from -- a second implementation, not the encoder's own word.
# encoder: flac 1.5.0
#
# Every accepted blob here declares 32,768 Hz, and so does every source WAV this
# file synthesizes. That is not incidental: since Q14 (ruled 2026-11-11) and plan
# item 7-0, `gafp_pack.py` refuses any stream whose declared rate is not the clock
# its measured rows are budgeted against, so an off-rate source could only ever
# reach this table as a refusal leg. `rate_44100_at_32768_target` is that leg, and
# the reason it is kept. A rate that *looks* close to the target — 32,000 Hz,
# 1.024x, +41.06 cents — is refused exactly like 44,100 Hz is: the declared rate is
# a validity check, never something the packer reinterprets.
#
# One block per committed blob under tests/gfp/, in the order gen_gafp_fixtures.py
# builds them, then the refusal legs. A block is: `# source:`/`# flags:`/`# why:`
# comments, the packer's own `profile`/`relaxations`/`verdict` data rows and any
# `# note:`/`# refused:` lines it has to say, then one `blob` row (file name, byte
# count, sha256, the manifest's own fields, and the PCM totals), then a `frame`
# row per frame and a `subframe` row per slot. Offsets in `region_offset` are RELATIVE TO THE START OF THE FRAME
# REGION -- that is what `Manifest::frame_region()` hands a caller -- and
# `blob_offset` is the absolute position, i.e. the value written to the offset
# table. The bit fields (`header_bits`, `entry_bit`, `exit_bit`, `padded`,
# `end_bit`) are ABSOLUTE bit positions in the source `.flac`, which includes the
# metadata before the frame region; they are not region-relative. No field value
# in a data row contains a space or an `=`, with one deliberate exception:
# `reason=`, which is quoted packer output and is therefore always the LAST field
# of its row. Prose lives in comment lines, so a reader in Rust can parse this
# without a parser.
#
# `pcm_fnv1a64` / `pcm_first` / `pcm_last` are the REFERENCE decoder's samples,
# hashed in the order and width the existing tables use: interleaved left-then-
# right, little-endian, 16-bit, FNV-1a 64 at the repo's offset basis
# 0xcbf43ce95de684b7 (`frame_vectors.fnv1a64`, mirrored in the Rust suites). The
# `blob` row's hash folds every frame; each `frame` row's hash starts fresh, so a
# wrong frame is localized as well as detected.
#
# Each block's `verdict` row is what the packer decided at the profile it built
# the blob at, and whether that profile is the C2 product one. The `refusal` rows
# below are the arms where it decided to write nothing at all; those have no file,
# and the witness is the exit status plus the reason it printed, keyed by a slug a
# Rust test can name.
#
# `sha256` is a provenance pin for people and for the generator's own `--check`
# (which compares committed bytes against a rebuild); the Rust suite pins `bytes=`
# and every frame's `bytes=` instead, because a hash function inside a test would
# be a second unverified thing in the gate. The PCM hashes below are the semantic
# pins, and they are computed by the Rust code.
#
# The three stereo rows share one `pcm_fnv1a64` by construction: same source PCM,
# three different frame sets (independent, mid/side, LPC). That is the shape of
# the witness the Rust suite runs — that identical decoder output can come from
# bytes that are not identical, and that the field the profile was supposed to be
# policed by (`max_fixed_order`) reads 0 in all three.

# ---- refusal legs: no file; the exit status and the printed reason are the witness ----
# why: the asset C2 cannot play, refused by the frames, not by a header field that reads 0
# wanted in the refusal: real LPC subframes ; decodes at 174.14% of the frame
refusal slug=lpc_at_product_profile exit=1 wrote_file=false reason=- real LPC subframes (order 4) x6: `-l 0` is the maximum LPC order the profile permits, and LPC is not what this target is built from - the asset uses lpc4 x6, and that predictor at this target decodes at 174.14% of the frame worst-case (bar set here at 50.0%, decode half only). measured 173.23% mean / 174.14% worst of the 1048576-cycle frame (1816753 cycles for 2048 samples at the 32768 Hz playback timer; the stream declares 32768 Hz, which is that clock, and the figure is keyed to the shape rather than the rate) — flac-docs/measurements.md, 6a-7b on hardware, `asm` arm, same instrument and same frames as the row above, `-l 4` arm: 1,816,753 c/frame = 173.23% mean / 174.14% worst. That arm's census is lpc4 x312 + lpc3 x2, so this is a CLIP mean and a LOWER bound on what the LPC kind alone costs per frame. Over budget by itself, before the producer's other stages exist. The flag that writes this anyway is --allow-over-budget, and it marks the blob NON-PRODUCT.
# why: a rate the container can express and this target has no measured path for — and, since Q14 and plan item 7-0, no interpretation either: the packer refuses it rather than budgeting it against a different clock. Note this is the native path — a WAV at 44,100 Hz would have been resampled to the target instead
# wanted in the refusal: sample rate 44100 Hz is not the target 32768 Hz
refusal slug=rate_44100_at_32768_target exit=1 wrote_file=false reason=- sample rate 44100 Hz is not the target 32768 Hz. Q14 (plan-of-record, ruled 2026-11-11): a stream is encoded at the rate it is played at, and this packer does not reinterpret a declared rate to fit the clock — the only reinterpretation it ever carried, 32,000 Hz onto a 32,768 Hz timer, is 1.024x, 41.06 cents sharp. The declared rate is also the clock every figure in MEASURED_DECODE is stated in, so a stream that declares another rate has no frame period to be measured against; re-encode it at 32768 Hz, or it is not a product asset. - frame 0 resolves a sample rate of 44100 Hz, not the 32768 Hz the stream was accepted at — a frame's 4-bit rate code is part of the bytes being packed, so a stream whose frames disagree with its own STREAMINFO is not the stream this profile was asked about (the 6b-3 respell trap) - frame 1 resolves a sample rate of 44100 Hz, not the 32768 Hz the stream was accepted at — a frame's 4-bit rate code is part of the bytes being packed, so a stream whose frames disagree with its own STREAMINFO is not the stream this profile was asked about (the 6b-3 respell trap) - frame 2 resolves a sample rate of 44100 Hz, not the 32768 Hz the stream was accepted at — a frame's 4-bit rate code is part of the bytes being packed, so a stream whose frames disagree with its own STREAMINFO is not the stream this profile was asked about (the 6b-3 respell trap) - frame 3 resolves a sample rate of 44100 Hz, not the 32768 Hz the stream was accepted at — a frame's 4-bit rate code is part of the bytes being packed, so a stream whose frames disagree with its own STREAMINFO is not the stream this profile was asked about (the 6b-3 respell trap)
# why: the depth the tests/README.md fixture list calls `8bit`: a refusal with a reason, arriving before any bytes are written
# wanted in the refusal: bits per sample 8 is outside the container's [16]
refusal slug=eight_bit_at_16bit exit=1 wrote_file=false reason=- bits per sample 8 is outside the container's [16] - verbatim x6: no measured decode figure for (2048-sample frames, verbatim) — the nearest measured row is (2048-sample frames, fixed, order 0): 42.48% mean, 42.72% worst, cited in flac-docs/measurements.md; measure it or pass --allow-unmeasured

# source: stereo_5000.wav
# flags: --channels 2 -L 4 --allow-lpc --allow-over-budget
# why: NOT a product blob, and the reason this file exists: the same source at `-l 4`. The packer needs TWO separate relaxations to write it — `--allow-lpc` for the profile limit (which preflight refuses up front, before encoding anything) and `--allow-over-budget` for the measured-cost bar — and the table records both, because `-L 4` is not the C2 profile. The product profile refuses this exact encode, and `--check` re-runs that refusal. Its manifest still reports max_fixed_order 0: that is the whole point of the 6b-2 witness.
